title: Tensor–Hom form of the exchange
statement:
Fix primes $p$ and $\ell\ne p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on the bounded constructible finite-Tor coefficient categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with its finite, completed integral, rationalized and common-stage coefficient conventions. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], with $Rf^!$ the constructible exceptional inverse image
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (no admissibility datum is assumed;
every such $f$ is exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility]), $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,N),
$$

natural in $M$ and $N$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension, and shifts. ([fix-lem-tensor-adjunction]; the
proof is the one given there, recalled here because the whole formal core
rests on it.)

proof.text: Write $H(P,Q)=R\mathcal Hom(P,Q)$ and $A_{M,N}=Rf_*H(M,f^!N)$, $B_{M,N}=H(Rf_!M,N)$. We first check that these are objects of the category on which Yoneda will be used. Axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum] is supplied on its displayed finite-Tor domains, so $f^!N$ and $Rf_!M$ belong to those domains. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, choose nonnegative dimension bounds for $X,Y$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], taking zero for an empty scheme. For either scheme $W$, [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite affine cover $U_i$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras; these are Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Here are the elementary chart checks used in applying the separated-scheme Hom theorem. The diagonal of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ over $k$ is closed because multiplication $B\otimes_k B\to B$ is surjective. An open immersion has isomorphic diagonal, hence is separated. On an affine chart of $W$, its intersection with $U_i$ is a quasi-compact open: each chart has Noetherian topology by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], and every open subset of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact (otherwise adjoining opens not covered by finitely many earlier ones produces a strictly ascending chain of opens). Cover the intersection by finitely many distinguished opens. Each $B_g$ is a finite-type $B$-algebra, generated by $g^{-1}$, so the finite-type definition applies to the inclusion. The bound for $W$ bounds each $U_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] therefore restricts the two inputs with unchanged Tor intervals. Apply [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] on each $U_i$ and identify its output with $H|_{U_i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. One bound $d_W$ for the finite affine family gives the common output interval $[c-b-2d_W,e-a+2d_W]$ for input Tor intervals $[a,b]$, $[c,e]$. Restriction to an open slice is exact: kernels and cokernels of sheaves restrict to the corresponding kernels and cokernels, since sheafification and its local equality test restrict to the same slice. Its derived tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These facts show that the Tor bound holds globally: every excluded cohomology sheaf restricts to zero on this cover. Constructibility also glues directly: intersect each finite local stratification with $U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$ to obtain a finite disjoint locally closed constructible stratification of $W$. The common Tor bound bounds the cohomology, by testing against the coefficient sheaf. Thus [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] put both internal Homs in $D^b_{ctf}$ without assuming that $X$ or $Y$ is separated over $k$. Finally [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], for the given separated finite-type $f$ and the dimension bound on $X$, puts $A_{M,N}$ in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$ as well. Empty schemes give zero objects.

source.place: Before Step 2: membership of the two represented objects; independent finite-coefficient domain check

proof.text: At $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, (A1) again supplies integral bounded constructible $f^!N$ and $Rf_!M$. Each of the two pairs defining $H$ has uniformly finite-Tor reductions by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]. [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] says that $H$ is derived complete and that its reductions are the finite internal Homs, preserving evaluation. Apply the finite affine-cover argument of step 1 at each level, with the same input intervals and the same dimension bounds. The resulting constructible reductions have one common Tor and cohomology interval. Hence [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] puts both internal Homs in the integral bounded constructible category, and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] puts them in $D^b_{ctf}$. The unconditional ordinary adjunction in clause (1) of [fix-prop-adjunctions] is an adjunction between the integral bounded constructible categories; in particular its $Rf_*$ takes the first internal Hom to $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] once more to obtain $A_{M,N}\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. This uses only the ordinary clause (1), not the conditional exceptional clause (2) of that node.

source.place: Before Step 2: integral domain check, with finite reductions and completed coefficient sheaves

proof.text: At $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] keeps the integral objects and replaces Hom groups by their tensor products with $E$. The operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] on objects are their integral constructions, followed by this rationalization. Thus the two objects of step 2 remain objects of the rationalized category. At $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents $M,N$ and the finitely many operations involved over a common finite coefficient field; apply the preceding membership check there. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] the finite-Tor field categories are precisely these bounded constructible categories. Thus at every coefficient stage both $A_{M,N}$ and $B_{M,N}$ lie in the full category $\mathcal C_Y=D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. The same definition identifies its Hom sets with the ambient Hom sets where an ambient realization is used.

source.place: Step 2: full finite-Tor category containing both represented objects at the field stages

proof.text:
Let $L$ range over $\mathcal C_Y$, exactly as in the current item proof. The tensor–internal-Hom adjunction is explicitly stated in [sk-def-sf-operations](i) for the derived operations at the coefficient stages of the datum. Together with (A1) and (A3) of [def-sf-datum], it gives natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,B_{M,N})
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^L L,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!(M\otimes^L Lf^*L),N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(M\otimes^L Lf^*L,f^!N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*L,H(M,f^!N))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,A_{M,N}).
\end{aligned}$$
The second bijection is precomposition with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}^{-1}$, with precisely the type specified by axiom (A3) of [def-sf-datum]. The more restricted notation node def-sf-pf is not needed here; no separatedness of the structure morphisms of $X$ and $Y$ is imposed. Its invertibility is the required axiom (A3), applicable because both $M,L$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible. At finite coefficients [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) put $M\otimes^L Lf^*L$ in the finite-Tor category; at integral coefficients use [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], and at the field stages use their specified coefficient constructions. Thus the third bijection uses the constructible exceptional adjunction (A1) on its domain. The fifth uses the ordinary adjunction (A1); the first and fourth use tensor–Hom. Every integral tensor here is completed tensor. Naturality of the adjunction bijections and the projection transformation makes this chain natural in $L$, contravariant in $M$, and covariant in $N$.

source.place: Step 1: the five Hom bijections, inverse projection formula, and the precise domains of the exceptional adjunction

proof.text: Denote the composite bijection in step 4 by $h_L:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Y}(L,B_{M,N})\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Y}(L,A_{M,N})$. Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the full category $\mathcal C_Y$, whose membership was established in steps 1–3. Explicitly set $a=h_B(1_B):B\to A$ and $b=h_A^{-1}(1_A):A\to B$. Naturality in $L$ gives $h_L(u)=a\circ u$ and $h_L^{-1}(v)=b\circ v$; applying the two inverse bijections shows $a\circ b=1_A$ and $b\circ a=1_B$. The required isomorphism has forward map $b:A\to B$. The bijection's naturality in $M,N$ implies the corresponding naturality equations for $b$ by the uniqueness in Yoneda. Since the finite-Tor category is full, this is also the claimed isomorphism in its ambient realization.

source.place: Tag 001P (categories-lemma-yoneda): fully faithful Yoneda on the full category containing both objects

proof.text: For a finite reduction or scalar-extension functor $T$, use the supplied coefficient comparisons of axiom (A5) in [def-sf-datum], on exactly the coefficient domains specified there. The forward map $b$ can be tested by transposing a morphism $u:L\to A$: transpose under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, then tensor–Hom, then $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, precompose with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}$, and transpose tensor–Hom again. This is $h_L^{-1}(u)$. Insert the coefficient comparisons before and after these five operations. Compatibility with the units and counits of (A1) and with the projection transformation (A3), required by (A5), makes the two composites equal; For the tensor/evaluation transpositions, integral reduction preserves evaluation by [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]. Finite quotient change uses the canonical global comparison defined as the transpose of the scalar-extended evaluation. On the separated affine cover of step 1, [thm-coef-finite-hom] says this comparison is an isomorphism. The restriction statement [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies its restrictions with those affine comparisons. Its cone restricts to zero on the cover, so its cohomology sheaves vanish globally, proving that the global comparison is invertible. Evaluation and transposition compatibility are its defining global adjunction identity, not a claim that equality of arbitrary derived morphisms can be detected on open restrictions. Integral scalar extension uses the natural operation comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. For the internal Hom, the comparison used is the canonical evaluation transpose $H_{\mathcal O_E}(P,Q)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\to H_{\mathcal O_L}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L,Q\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)$, and it is invertible: by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] the completed coefficient sheaf $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ is finite free of rank $[L:E]$ over $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and, for derived complete objects, integral scalar extension is ordinary change of rings $-\otimes^L_RS$. After choosing a basis, $H_S(P\otimes_RS,Q\otimes_RS)\cong H_R(P,Q\otimes_RS)\cong H_R(P,Q)\otimes_RS$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $H_R(P,Q)$, and the evaluation transpose is this identification, independent of the basis. So it is an isomorphism with the same objects as the comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Their evaluation equation is the balancing equation $(x\otimes a)\otimes(h\otimes b)\mapsto h(x)\otimes ab$ on the tensor–Hom pairing, and the same equation at each finite reduction defines the completed comparison. The quotient and scalar maps are therefore the evaluation-defined tensor–Hom comparisons, rather than arbitrary chosen isomorphisms. Thus the two paths around the exchange comparison square have the same transpose, and injectivity of the Hom bijections makes the paths equal. This checks the actual morphism $b$, not just its isomorphism class. At rational coefficients the equations are the integral equations tensored with the coefficient field, using [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. At algebraically closed coefficients they hold over a common finite field and hence in the Hom colimit of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the scalar-extension comparison cocycles make them independent of the representative. Only the comparisons supplied at their stated stages are used; no reduction from rational coefficients to a finite quotient is invoked.

source.place: Step 2: naturality and finite-reduction/scalar-extension compatibilities of the ingredients

proof.text: For shifts, use the signed internal-Hom comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]: $H(P[r],Q)=H(P,Q)[-r]$ and $H(P,Q[r])=H(P,Q)[r]$. Under these comparisons the chain for $(L,N[r])$ is the chain for $(L[-r],N)$; the right-adjoint shift comparisons are defined by transposing the shift comparisons of the left adjoints. To check the projection arrow rather than assume its shift compatibility, use its explicit construction [def-exchange-projection]: the proper projection map is the transpose of $(\varepsilon_p\otimes1)\circ\mu_p$, and the compact-support projection is its composite with $Rp_*(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is the open-extension tensor comparison and pullback composition. Shifting a tensor factor shifts this composite by the total-tensor convention, with $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^r d_C$; the tensor–Hom evaluation comparison uses the same signed convention. The two shifted transposition routes therefore agree. At integral coefficients the inverse-limit functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so the same comparisons pass through the completed pullback and tensor constructions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Rationalization and common finite stages have their induced shifts by the definitions cited in step 3. Consequently $h$ for shifted arguments is the shifted $h$, and the uniqueness in step 5 gives the shift square for $b$ in $N$, and in $M$ with the negative internal-Hom shift.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated
finite-type morphism, with $Rf^!$ the constructible exceptional inverse image
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (no admissibility datum is assumed;
every such $f$ is exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility]), $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,N),
$$

natural in $M$ and $N$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension, and shifts.

proof.text:
The adjunctions and the projection transformation used throughout are
those recorded in [fix-prop-adjunctions] and
[fix-lem-tensor-adjunction], in the form fixed by [def-sf-pf].
Step 1: for every $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the adjunctions of axiom
(A1) and the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give the chain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(L,R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,N)\bigr)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^L_\Lambda L,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(Rf_!(M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L),N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L,f^!N\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X\bigl(Lf^*L,R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\bigr)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y\bigl(L,Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!N)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$

the second isomorphism being the *inverse* of the projection formula
(axiom (A3), [def-sf-pf]), the third the adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, and the first, fourth and fifth the tensor–internal-Hom
adjunction together with $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. Step 2: the chain is natural
in $L$, so the two objects represent the same functor on
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$; the Yoneda lemma applied to degree-zero morphisms
of that triangulated category gives the canonical isomorphism, whose
naturality and compatibilities are those of the ingredients.
